title: A people without gods needed prophets
source_text: Λεγέτωσαν δὴ ἡμῖν ὁ Κέλσος καὶ οἱ ἀρεσκόμενοι τοῖς καθ᾿ ἡμῶν ὑπ᾿ αὐτοῦ λεγομένοις, εἰ ὄνου σκιᾷ ἔοικε τὸ προειρηκέναι τοὺς Ἰουδαίων προφήτας τόπον γενέσεως τοῦ ἡγησομένου τῶν καλῶς βεβιωκότων καὶ τῶν χρηματιζόντων μερίδος θεοῦ καὶ παρθένον συλληψομένην τὸν Ἐμμανουὴλ καὶ σημεῖα καὶ τεράστια ἐσόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ προφητευομένου τοιάδε, καὶ ὅτι „ἕως τάχους δραμεῖται ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ.“ ὡς „εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν“ ἐξελθεῖν τὸν φθόγγον αὐτοῦ τῶν ἀποστόλων, τίνα τε πείσεται ὑπὸ Ἰουδαίων καταδικαζόμενος καὶ πῶς ἀναστήσεται. ἆρα γὰρ ὡς ἔτυχε ταῦτ᾿ ἔλεγον οἱ προφῆται σὺν οὐδεμιᾷ πιθανότητι. τῇ κινούσῃ αὐτοὺς ἐπὶ τὸ μὴ μόνον εἰπεῖν ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀναγραφῆς ἀξιῶσαι τὰ λεγόμενα; ἆρα δὲ τὸ τοσοῦτο τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος, πάλαι χώραν ἰδίαν εἰληφὸς οἰκεῖν. σὺν οὐδεμιᾷ πιθανότητι τινὰς μὲν ὡς προφήτας ἀνηγόρευον ἑτέρους δὲ ὡς ψευδοπροφήτας ἀπεδοκίμαζον; καὶ οὐδὲν ἦν παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς τὸ προκαλούμενον συναριθμεῖν ταῖς ἱεραῖς εἶναι πεπιστευμέναις Μωϋσέως βίβλοις τοὺς λόγους τῶν ἑξῆς νενομισμένων εἶναι προφητῶν; καὶ δύνανται ἡμῖν παραστῆσαι οἱ εὐήθειαν ἐγκαλοῦντες Ἰουδαίοις καὶ Χριστιανοῖς ὅτι ἐδύνατο συνεστηκέναι τὸ Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος, μηδεμιᾶς ἐπαγγελίας προγνώσεων οὔσης παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς. καὶ ὅτι τὰ μὲν περὶ αὐτοὺς ἔθνη [ᾗ] ἕκαστον κατὰ τὰ πάτρια ἐπίστευε χρησμοὺς λαμβάνειν καὶ μαντείας ἀπὸ τῶν παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς νομιζομένων θεῶν, οὗτοι δὲ μόνοι, οἱ διδαχθέντες πάντων τῶν παρὰ τοῖς ἔθνεσι νομιζομένων θεῶν καταφρονεῖν ὡς οὐ θεῶν ἀλλὰ δαιμονίων (ἐπεὶ ἔλεγον αὐτῶν οἱ προφῆται τὸ „πάντες οἱ θεοὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν δαιμόνια“), οὐδένα τὸν ἐπαγγελλόμενον εἶχον προφητεύειν καὶ δυνάμενον περισπᾶν τοὺς πόθῳ προγνώσεως τῶν μελλόντων αὐτομολεῖν (βουλομένους) πρὸς τοὺς παρὰ τοῖς ἄλλοις δαίμονας; ἐπίστησον οὖν εἰ μὴ ἀναγκαῖόν ἐστιν ὅλον ἔθνος διδασκόμενον καταφρονεῖν τῶν παρὰ τοῖς λοιποῖς θεῶν εὐπορηκέναι προφητῶν, τὸ μεῖζον αὐτόθεν ἐμφαινόντων καὶ τὸ ὑπερέχον τὰ πανταχοῦ χρηστήρια.
pass_a_gloss: Let Celsus and those pleased (ἀρέσκω) with the things said by him against us tell us whether it is like (ἔοικα) an ass’s shadow (ὄνου σκιά) that the prophets of the Jews foretold (προλέγω) the place of birth (γένεσις) of the one who will lead (ἡγέομαι) those who have lived (βιόω) well and those bearing the name (χρηματίζω) of God’s portion (μερίς), and a virgin (παρθένος) who will conceive (συλλαμβάνω) Emmanuel, and such signs (σημεῖον) and wonders (τέρας, τεράστιον) to be done by the one prophesied, and that ‘his word (λόγος) will run (τρέχω) with speed (ἕως τάχους)’, so that the voice (φθόγγος) of his apostles went out ‘into all the earth’, and what he will suffer (πάσχω) being condemned (καταδικάζω) by Jews, and how he will rise (ἀνίστημι). Did the prophets then say these things at random (ὡς ἔτυχε) with no persuasiveness (πιθανότης) moving (κινέω) them not only to say but also to deem worthy of writing (ἀναγραφή) the things said? And did so great a nation (ἔθνος) of the Jews, long ago having received a land (χώρα) of its own to dwell in, with no persuasiveness proclaim (ἀναγορεύω) some as prophets and reject (ἀποδοκιμάζω) others as false prophets (ψευδοπροφήτης)? And was there nothing among them inviting (προκαλέομαι) [them] to number together (συναριθμέω) with the books of Moses, believed to be sacred (ἱερός), the words of those afterwards held (νομίζω) to be prophets? And can those charging (ἐγκαλέω) foolishness (εὐήθεια) on Jews and Christians show (παρίστημι) us that the nation of the Jews could have held together (συνίστημι), there being no promise (ἐπαγγελία) of foreknowledge (πρόγνωσις) among them; and that the nations around them each according to ancestral [customs] believed they received oracles (χρησμός) and divinations (μαντεία) from those held gods among them, but these alone, taught to despise (καταφρονέω) all those held gods among the nations as not gods but demons (δαιμόνιον) (since their prophets said ‘all the gods of the nations are demons’), had no one professing (ἐπαγγέλλομαι) to prophesy and able to draw away (περισπάω) those wishing, by longing (πόθος) for foreknowledge of things to come, to desert (αὐτομολέω) to the demons among the others? Consider (ἐφίστημι) then whether it is not necessary that a whole nation taught to despise the gods among the rest had plenty (εὐπορέω) of prophets, showing (ἐμφαίνω) at once (αὐτόθεν) what is greater and what surpasses (ὑπερέχω) the oracles (χρηστήριον) everywhere.
pass_b_english: Let Celsus, then, and those who are pleased with what he says against us, tell us whether it is like the shadow of an ass that the prophets of the Jews foretold the birthplace of him who would lead those who have lived good lives and those who are called God’s portion (Micah 5:2; Matthew 2:6; Deuteronomy 32:9); that a virgin would conceive Emmanuel (Isaiah 7:14); that such signs and wonders would be done by the one prophesied; that “his word will run swiftly” (Psalm 147:15), so that the voice of his apostles went out “into all the earth” (Psalm 19:4; Romans 10:18); and what he would suffer when condemned by the Jews, and how he would rise again.

Did the prophets say these things at random, with no convincing reason to move them not only to speak but also to judge their words worthy of being written down? And did so great a nation as the Jews, which long ago received a land of its own to dwell in, with no convincing reason proclaim some men as prophets and reject others as false prophets? Was there nothing among them that moved them to number the words of the later men who were held to be prophets with the books of Moses, which were believed to be sacred?

And can those who accuse Jews and Christians of foolishness show us that the nation of the Jews could have held together if there had been no promise of foreknowledge among them? Can they show that, while the nations around them each believed, according to their ancestral customs, that they received oracles and divinations from those they held to be gods, these alone, who had been taught to despise all the gods held by the nations as being not gods but demons (for their prophets said, “All the gods of the nations are demons” (Psalm 96:5)), had no one who professed to prophesy and who could hold back those who, out of longing to know the future beforehand, wished to desert to the demons of the other peoples?

Consider, then, whether it was not necessary that a whole nation taught to despise the gods of the other peoples should have had an abundance of prophets, who by that very fact showed something greater, surpassing the oracles found everywhere.

choices.choice: Copy-text: staged source_3.json section 2 (Koetschau 3.2). The birthplace of the leader is Micah 5:2 (Hebrew 5:1), whose ‘ἡγούμενος’ wording Origen echoes as quoted in Matthew 2:6; ‘those called God’s portion’ echoes Deuteronomy 32:9 (‘the Lord’s portion is his people’), cited as a clear allusion. ‘ἕως τάχους δραμεῖται ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ’ is LXX Psalm 147:4, which is Psalm 147:15 in English Bibles (LXX 147 = Hebrew 147:12–20). ‘εἰς πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν’ is LXX Psalm 18:5 = English Psalm 19:4, applied to the apostles as in Romans 10:18. ‘πάντες οἱ θεοὶ τῶν ἐθνῶν δαιμόνια’ is LXX Psalm 95:5 = English Psalm 96:5 (the Hebrew reads ‘idols’). The staged text reads ‘τὸν φθόγγον αὐτοῦ τῶν ἀποστόλων’; taken as ‘the voice of his apostles’ (some would read αὐτῶν, ‘their voice, that of the apostles’; the sense is the same). The prophesied signs and wonders, sufferings and resurrection are general and not tied to one verse here (Origen gave the texts in Books 1–2), so no further inline citation. The bracketed ‘[ᾗ]’ is an editorial deletion and is not translated; ‘(βουλομένους)’ is an editorial supplement and is translated (‘wished’). The plural verbs with ‘ἔθνος’ (ἀνηγόρευον, ἀπεδοκίμαζον) are rendered with the singular ‘nation’. The long Greek question ‘δύνανται … παραστῆσαι … ὅτι … καὶ ὅτι …’ is split into two questions with the same verb repeated (‘Can they show that …’). ‘τῶν ἑξῆς νενομισμένων εἶναι προφητῶν’ rendered ‘the later men who were held to be prophets’ (ἑξῆς marks the prophets who came after Moses, not a later change of opinion).
word order: ‘Let Celsus, then, and those who … tell us’
‘would do such and such signs’ made ‘such signs and wonders would be done by the one prophesied’ (τοιάδε, ἐσόμενα ὑπό)
‘the great nation’ made ‘so great a nation as the Jews’ (τὸ τοσοῦτο ἔθνος)
‘those who were afterwards held to be prophets’ made ‘the later men who were held to be prophets’ (τῶν ἑξῆς), removing a false sense of later recognition

Scripture citations rechecked: Micah 5:2 / Matthew 2:6 (ἡγούμενος), Deuteronomy 32:9 (μερίς), Isaiah 7:14, LXX Ps 147:4 = Psalm 147:15, LXX Ps 18:5 = Psalm 19:4 with Romans 10:18, LXX Ps 95:5 = Psalm 96:5; all correct
